title: Re-roll: a fresh hand for Royal Valley
question: Every earlier direction is out. The roll assigned Event Wayfinding. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: This Way to Royal Valley
options.lineage: 1970s transit & airport pictogram signage, event wayfinding boards
options.thesis: Guests at every event already follow one sign: RESTROOMS →. The site is built as that signage system, enamel sign panels, pictograms, and arrows that lead straight to booking.
options.viewport: A full-width royal-blue sign panel: three door pictograms over '3 stations', the line 'Luxury restrooms → Walla Walla & nearby' at signage scale, the night trailer photo as the place the arrow points, and a yellow 'Book your date →' panel beside both phone numbers.
options.risk: Signage grammar is cool and civic; done timidly it reads like an airport, not a wedding.

raised.raise: The three stations are drawn as three identical repeated units, the row itself is the measure.
Sections are stacked as distinct sign panels separated by deep, honest gaps of ground.
Buttons physically depress like push-plates on press, with a short settle.
One type family at strictly two sizes per panel; hierarchy comes from the panel, not from type tricks.
Every photo shown full-frame and unretouched, as the place the sign leads to.

options.label: Boutique Hotel Amenity Program
options.lineage: boutique hotel key tags, door hangers, amenity cards
options.thesis: The trailer as a hotel suite you can tow: key-tag navigation, a door hanger that flips VACANT/OCCUPIED, amenities on a turndown card.
options.viewport: A door hanger hanging over the night photo, flipping to VACANT, with the Book button as the room key.
options.risk: Close to the familiar hotel-luxury look many rentals already borrow.

options.label: Fight Poster
options.thesis: ROYAL VALLEY vs. THE PORTA-POTTY: two contenders face off across a gold VS, specs as the tale of the tape.
options.viewport: Split sheet: the trailer photo vs. a standard portable toilet, A/C, sink, lights tallied down each side.
options.case: Comparison makes the value instantly clear; loses audience identification with weddings and corporate hosts.
options.risk: Punchy humor can cheapen the luxury promise.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: A row of needles leaning into the red.
options.case: No audience link to restrooms or events.
options.kept: Identical repeated units as the row's ruler (the three stations).

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.case: Dreamlike, says nothing about the product.
options.kept: Sections as stacked blocks with deep gaps between.

options.label: Rubber-Hose Cel
options.viewport: Iris opening on a cartoon trailer.

options.label: Hand-Processed 16mm
options.case: Arty degradation fights a clean-and-comfortable promise.

options.label: Cracktro Void
options.viewport: One line of text in a void.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Luxury restroom trailer site: dark photo hero, gold accents, amenity icons, gallery, contact form, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Night trailer photo full-bleed, headline, Book Now button, three amenity columns below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other luxury-trailer rental by design.
